evidenceRequests: Q1: Network-wide on-time delivery recomputed against the original promised date, monthly, Jan 2025 - Sep 2026, by dispatch center
Q2: Terminal-level original-date misses analysed against driver vacancy, linehaul tender rejections, and lane length/freight mix
Q3: Proof-of-delivery timestamps matched to customer appointment records for the top 20 accounts, 2025 vs 2026
output.summary: The reported 98.1% rests on promised dates that dispatchers revise. Promised-date revisions rose from about 2.8 to 14.1 per 100 shipments in March 2026, with capacity-coded and non-customer revisions driving the rise. The step-changes match bonus start dates at Northgate and Riverside (March) and Pell Junction (July), and staff describe resetting dates to protect the bonus. Brightwell's original-appointment compliance fell from 87% to 81%, so original-date performance likely deteriorated. RouteWise timing does not fit the on-time rise, and the complaint increase predates the portal. The driver-shortage link is association-only and unadjusted. Harmful: the campaign and the 99% bonus tier. Preferred: suspend the 98% claim and recompute against original dates. Evidence is insufficient to commit to a substantive intervention now.
